name: GPCRdb_get_protein
description: Get detailed GPCR protein information from GPCRdb. Returns receptor family, species, sequence, and classification. GPCRs are targets of ~35% of approved drugs. No authentication required.

protein.description: Protein entry name (e.g., adrb2_human for beta-2 adrenergic receptor) or UniProt accession (e.g., P07550)

receptor_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

protein_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

genes.description: Gene symbols for the receptor, e.g. ['ADRB2'].

receptor_class.description: GPCR class, e.g. 'Class A (Rhodopsin)'. Classes have different architectures, so a class is what says whether a structural comparison is meaningful.

residue_numbering_scheme.description: The generic numbering scheme the residue numbers follow, e.g. 'GPCRdb(A)'. Generic numbers are only comparable within one scheme; read under the wrong one they point at the wrong residue.

sequence.description: The receptor's amino-acid sequence. Residue positions are indices into it.

source.description: Where the entry came from, e.g. 'SWISSPROT' or 'TREMBL'. A TrEMBL entry is unreviewed.

name: GPCRdb_list_proteins
description: List GPCR protein families or proteins in a specific family from GPCRdb. Without family parameter, returns list of protein families (Class A, Class B, etc.). With family parameter (e.g., '001') or protein_class (e.g., 'Chemokine receptors'), returns proteins in that family. No authentication required.

protein_class.description: Human-readable GPCR class or family name (e.g., 'Chemokine receptors', 'Class A', 'Adrenergic'). Alias for family that accepts plain English names.

family.description: GPCR family code (e.g., '001' for Class A Rhodopsin, '002' for Class B). If not provided, lists all protein families.
Which family was listed, e.g. 'all families'. What the reply actually covers.

note.description: How to narrow the listing - that a family's numeric slug must be passed as 'family'. The instruction that turns an unusable whole-database listing into a targeted one.

name: GPCRdb_get_structures
description: Get GPCR crystal/cryo-EM structures from GPCRdb. Returns PDB codes, resolution, receptor state (active/inactive), and bound ligands. Filter by protein or receptor state.

protein.description: Protein entry name (optional - returns all structures if not specified)

state.description: Receptor state filter: active, inactive, intermediate

resolution.description: Maximum resolution in Angstroms (client-side filter, e.g., 2.5 returns only structures ≤2.5Å)

receptor_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

protein_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

protein.description: The receptor the structures belong to, e.g. 'adrb2_human'. Echoes what the query resolved to.

state_filter.description: Which activation states were included, e.g. 'all'. Active and inactive GPCR structures differ substantially, so a list without this cannot be interpreted.

name: GPCRdb_get_ligands
description: Get ligands associated with a GPCR from GPCRdb. Returns ligand names, types (agonist/antagonist), and binding data. Essential for GPCR drug discovery.

receptor_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

protein_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

type.description: Ligand class filter (e.g., small molecule, peptide, antibody).

ligand_type.description: Alias for type. Ligand class filter (e.g., small molecule, peptide).

limit.description: Maximum number of ligands to return (default: all). Use to cap large result sets.

max_results.description: Alias for limit. Maximum number of ligands to return.

note.description: How to narrow the listing - that a family's numeric slug must be passed as 'family'. The instruction that turns an unusable whole-database listing into a targeted one.

name: GPCRdb_get_mutations
description: Get mutation data for a GPCR from GPCRdb. Returns mutation positions, effects on ligand binding and signaling. Useful for understanding structure-function relationships.

receptor_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

protein_name.description: Alias for protein. GPCRdb entry name (e.g., adrb2_human).

note.description: How to narrow the listing - that a family's numeric slug must be passed as 'family'. The instruction that turns an unusable whole-database listing into a targeted one.
